name: Professional Employment Visa
description: The E-7 visa is designed for foreign professionals with specialized skills working for Korean companies. It covers a wide range of professional categories from IT to engineering to management.
tagline: For skilled professionals building their career in Korea
keyRequirement: Job offer from a Korean company + bachelor's degree (or 5+ years experience)

eligibility.label: Valid job offer from Korean company
Bachelor's degree or higher in related field
Relevant work experience
eligibility.description: Usually 1+ years for degree holders, 5+ years without degree

eligibility.label: Salary meeting minimum threshold
eligibility.description: Must meet or exceed industry standards

fees.notes: Multiple entry visa may have additional fees

incomeRequirement.notes: Must meet or exceed the average salary for your occupation category. IT professionals typically need ₩40,000,000+ annually.

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Must be valid for duration of employment contract

documents.name: Employment Contract
documents.description: Signed contract from Korean employer showing position, salary, and duration

documents.name: Degree Certificate
documents.description: Original or certified copy, apostilled if from foreign country
tips: Must be in related field to your job

documents.name: Career Certificate / Employment History
tips: Get reference letters from previous employers

documents.name: Tax Payment Certificates (for extensions)
documents.description: Proof of tax payments in Korea

applicationSteps.title: Secure Job Offer
applicationSteps.description: Receive and sign employment contract from Korean company.
tips: Negotiate salary - it affects visa approval
Ensure company is willing to sponsor visa

applicationSteps.title: Employer Prepares Documents
applicationSteps.description: Company prepares business registration, tax certificates, and sponsorship documents.

applicationSteps.title: Prepare Personal Documents
applicationSteps.description: Gather degree certificates, career documents, and get apostilles if needed.

applicationSteps.title: Submit Application
applicationSteps.description: Apply at Korean embassy/consulate (if abroad) or immigration office (if in Korea).

applicationSteps.title: Wait for Visa Issuance Number
applicationSteps.description: Immigration reviews application. Employer may receive VIN for you.

applicationSteps.title: Get Visa Stamp / Enter Korea
applicationSteps.description: Pick up visa at embassy, or if already in Korea, receive ARC.

processingTime.notes: Processing times vary by nationality and occupation category

restrictions: Must work for sponsoring employer only
Job changes require new visa/employer sponsorship
workPermission.notes: You can change employers, but must update visa accordingly

faqs.question: Can I change jobs on an E-7 visa?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you must report the change to immigration and get your visa updated with the new employer as sponsor. Don't start working for the new company until this is complete.

faqs.question: What if my company goes bankrupt?
faqs.answer: A grace period may be granted (typically 30 days, but varies by case). Confirm with immigration authorities. You can change to D-10 (job seeking) visa if you need more time.

faqs.question: Can my family come to Korea?
faqs.answer: Yes, your spouse and children can apply for F-3 (dependent) visas. They cannot work unless they get separate work authorization.

faqs.question: Can I become a permanent resident?
faqs.answer: After 3+ years on E-7, you may be eligible for F-2-7 (points-based residence visa) or F-5 (permanent residence) depending on your points.

faqs.question: What salary do I need?
faqs.answer: There's no fixed minimum, but your salary should meet or exceed the average for your occupation. Immigration checks this. For IT, expect at least ₩40-50 million annually.

tips: Negotiate salary before signing - higher salary improves visa chances
Large, established companies have smoother visa processes
Keep all employment documents - you'll need them for extensions
Start extension process 2 months before visa expires
Build good relationship with HR - they handle visa paperwork
Consider F-2 visa after 3 years for more flexibility
warnings: Working without proper visa is grounds for deportation
Don't start working until visa is approved
Changing jobs without updating visa is a violation

pathsTo.name: Residence Visa (F-2-7 Points-Based)
pathsTo.requirements: Score 80+ on the F-2-7 points system. Typically need 3+ years on E-7, income above GNI average, TOPIK score, and other point categories.
pathsTo.notes: The most desirable upgrade from E-7. F-2 removes employer-tied restrictions — you can change jobs freely, freelance, or start a business. Start preparing early: take TOPIK, build work history, complete KIIP courses for bonus points.

pathsTo.name: Job Seeking Visa
pathsTo.requirements: Between jobs (company closure, contract end, layoff). Apply during the grace period before E-7 expires.
pathsTo.notes: A fallback option if you lose your job. Grace period is typically 30 days but varies. Apply immediately — do not wait until the last minute. D-10 gives you up to 2 years to find new employment.

pathsFrom.name: Student Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Secure a job offer from a Korean company in your field. Must have completed your degree.
pathsFrom.notes: Can transition directly if you have a job offer, or go through D-10 first. Many Korean university graduates find jobs through campus recruitment events.

pathsFrom.name: Intra-Company Transfer Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Change from intra-company assignment to direct employment with a Korean entity. New employer must sponsor.
pathsFrom.notes: Common for employees who were transferred to Korea and decide to join a local company directly.

pathsFrom.name: Job Seeking Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Secure a job offer from a Korean company. Employer must be willing to sponsor E-7 visa.
pathsFrom.timeline: 2-4 weeks processing after employer submits documents
pathsFrom.notes: The primary path from D-10 to employment. Your new employer handles most of the sponsorship paperwork. Large companies generally have smoother processes.

pathsFrom.name: English Teaching Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Secure a professional job offer outside of teaching. Must meet E-7 qualification requirements (degree + experience in relevant field).
pathsFrom.notes: Common for English teachers who want to transition to professional work. May need additional qualifications or experience depending on the target profession.

pathsFrom.name: Digital Nomad Visa (Workcation)
pathsFrom.requirements: Secure a job offer from a Korean company. Must give up remote work arrangement or maintain it separately.
pathsFrom.notes: For digital nomads who find local employment opportunities. Note: you can no longer work for foreign companies on E-7. This is a significant lifestyle change.

pathsFrom.name: Overseas Korean Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Secure a job offer from a Korean company. F-4 holders already have work authorization but E-7 may be needed for specific employer sponsorship situations.
pathsFrom.notes: F-4 holders already have broad work rights, so this transition is less common. Usually only needed for specific regulatory or company requirements.

pathsFrom.name: Working Holiday Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Secure a professional job offer before H-1 expires. Must meet E-7 qualification requirements.
pathsFrom.notes: Possible but less common directly from H-1. Most go through D-10 first. Start job searching early — H-1 cannot be extended.
